title: Expression and purification of phage T7 ejection proteins for cryo-EM analysis
protocol: Follow the before you begin protocol to optimize expression of internal virion proteins starting from fresh transformations of pET16-b_gp15 and pET16-b_gp16 in BL21-LOBSTR(DE3).
Complete the before you begin protocol purification of soluble ejection proteins T7 gp15 and gp16 for 6 L LB each.
Pool fractions of purified gp15 separately from those of purified gp16.
Concentrate gp15 using a 30 kDa MWCO centrifugal filter concentrator to ∼1–2 mg/mL.
Check the protein absorbance at 280 nm throughout the concentration process of gp15.
Concentrate gp16 using a 50 kDa MWCO centrifugal filter concentrator to ∼5 mg/mL.
Check the protein absorbance at 280 nm throughout the concentration process of gp16.
Mix gp15 and gp16 in a 3:1 molar ratio in GF buffer-I.
Incubate the mixture on ice for 1 hour.
Concentrate the sample to one-third of the total volume using a 100 kDa MWCO centrifugal filter concentrator.
Mix by pipetting up and down gently during concentration intervals.
Inject the complex sample on a calibrated analytical Superose 6 10/300 GL column equilibrated in GF buffer-I.
Estimate the molecular weight of the resulting peaks.
Observe a shift for larger MW species compared to individual components.
Run an SDS-PAGE gel for “inject” and peak fractions alongside a molecular weight standard.
Determine complex formation for fractions containing both components.
Optional: For further evidence of interaction between DNA-ejectosome components gp15 and gp16, run a NativePAGE (Invitrogen) with individual components versus the complex.
Observe shifts in band migration.
Follow manufacturer’s protocol for gel running conditions.
Store the T7 periplasmic tunnel complex at 4°C or on ice until use.
Use within 1–3 days post-complex formation to avoid loss due to aggregation.
Turn on current amplifier (Keithley 428) one hour before the measurements.
Prepare lipid solution before experiments according to protocol.
Clean measuring cuvette according to protocol.
Take 3 μL of priming lipid solution and apply around aperture at the back side.
Let chloroform evaporate for 15 minutes.
Take 2 μL of priming lipid solution and apply around aperture at the front side.
Let chloroform evaporate for 15 minutes.
Clean Ag/AgCl electrodes with water.
Clean Ag/AgCl electrodes with ethanol.
Dry Ag/AgCl electrodes by blotting with absorbent paper.
Clean electrodes by bathing them in pepsin solution for 2 h and then rinse well with water when switching from one protein to another.
Fill the measuring cuvette with 10 mL of electrolyte solution (1 M KCl, 10 mM HEPES, pH 7.4).
Place electrodes into the measuring cuvette.
Set power source to 10 mV for voltage source test and measure the voltage output using a voltmeter connected to the trans side, it should be 10 ± 0.5 mV.
Perform zero voltage test without applying voltage and bridged electrodes, the reading should be 0 mV ± 0.03 mV.
Set voltage to -10 mV for electrode asymmetry test.
Measure electrode asymmetry without applied voltage and without bridging.
Set up Keithley 428 current amplifier with gain of 106 V/A for membrane painting.
Set up Keithley 428 current amplifier with gain of 109 V/A for experiment recording.
Apply 3 μL of the painting lipid solution on the Teflon loop.
Slowly and gently move the loop up and down across the aperture to form a membrane.
Observe the appearance of black color in the aperture using light source and scope.
Assess membrane stability: Produce three separate membranes and record them for at least 15 minutes.
Add protein sample buffer to both sides of the cuvette once a stable baseline is recorded.
Record three membranes for at least 15 minutes each after adding the buffer.
Test the protein sample by adding gp14 to both sides of the cuvette.
Record at least 100 insertions from several membranes.
If no insertions are observed, paint new membrane and increase protein concentration in the cuvette.
Determine optimal concentration of the protein for further experiments.
Analyze recorded data using IGOR Pro 5.03.
Make graphs with SigmaPlot 11.0.
Dilute purified individual components or gp15:gp16 complex to 0.01–0.05 mg/mL in the final gel filtration buffer or distilled water for negative stain sample preparation.
Glow discharge 2–4 nm carbon-coated 300 or 400-mesh copper grids (EMS) for 2 min at 25 mA in a vacuum chamber with the carbon-side facing up.
Pipette 2–4 μl of diluted sample onto the glow-discharged grid and allow adsorption for 1 min.
Pipette three 25 μL droplets of distilled water on a clean sheet of parafilm.
Pipette two 25 μL droplets of 2% uranyl acetate on the same sheet.
Blot excess sample from the grid with filter paper, touching only the edges at a 90-degree angle.
Quickly dab the carbon-side of the grid on each water droplet to wash it.
Hold the carbon-side of the grid on the first 2% uranyl acetate stain droplet for 10 seconds.
Blot excess stain from the grid with filter paper.
Hold the carbon-side of the grid on the second 2% uranyl acetate stain droplet for 1 minute.
Blot excess stain again to remove any remaining liquid.
Allow the grid to air-dry for at least 5 minutes before use.
Load grids into a transmission electron microscope operated at 100–200 kV.
Observe sample particle distribution, purity, aggregation levels, conformational flexibility and heterogeneity of shape and size.
Record micrographs for particle size analysis using ImageJ or processing with Relion for particle picking and 2D class average generation.
Proceed to cryo-EM if sample quality is good (i.e., homogeneous particles, evenly distributed, with little to no aggregation).
Turn on the vitrobot and attach blotting paper to the blotting pads inside the climate chamber.
Set the temperature and humidity of the climate chamber to 4°C and 100 percent humidity, respectively.
Set blotting parameters on the control screen.
Fill the coolant container peripheral ring with liquid nitrogen.
Allow all metal components to equilibrate in the coolant container.
Mix liquid ethane and pour it into the central cup of the coolant container.
Wait until the ethane becomes cloudy before removing the metal spindle.
Load the cooled coolant container onto the platform ring.
Top off the peripheral ring with liquid nitrogen during use.
Dilute purified individual components or gp15:gp16 complex to 1 mg/mL in final gel filtration buffer or distilled water.
Glow discharge 300-mesh Quantifoil 1.2/1.3 holey carbon grids for 30 seconds at 25 mA with the carbon-side facing up.
Place a grid on tweezers and raise the tweezer arm and coolant chamber using the control screen or foot pedal.
Pipette 2.5 μL of 1 mg/mL sample through the sample port onto the grid.
Allow adsorption for 10–60 seconds.
Adjust blotting parameters on the control screen for each grid/sample.
Initiate the blotting/plunging procedure from the control screen or use the foot pedal.
Disconnect the tweezers from the central axis without letting the grid touch the sides of the central cup.
Transfer the grid from the central cup to the peripheral ring filled with liquid nitrogen.
Drop the grid into a slot of a grid storage box.
Discard any bent grids.
Load grids into cryo-electron microscope operated at 200 kV–300 kV.
Observe ice conditions, sample particle distribution, purity, aggregation levels, conformational flexibility and heterogeneity of shape and size.
Record micrographs for particle size analysis using ImageJ or processing with Relion for particle picking and 2D class average generation.
Proceed to cryo-EM data collection if grid and sample quality is good (i.e., homogeneous particles, evenly distributed, with little to no aggregation).
